newsitem.title: USA: Government says flu season waning.
newsitem.headline: Government says flu season waning.

text.p: Influenza activity has declined during the past month, but almost every state was still reporting flu cases, federal health officials said Thursday.

The Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said 21 states reported flu outbreaks during the week ending Feb. 15, two fewer than the previous week. Another 25 states and the District of Columbia were reporting some influenza cases.
The CDC said flu was widespread in Alaska, Arizona, Iowa, Nevada, Vermont and Virginia. There was no reported flu activity in Colorado, Maine, Rhode Island and Wyoming.
The flu season peaked in late December, the agency said. Deaths from pneumonia and influenza in selected cities reached a peak in late January. The flu season usually ends in April.
An average of about 20,000 Americans die from influenza or its complications every year, the CDC said.
